faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or occupations and are often higher. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, but many awards pay more. Casual employees also receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate. Always check the relevant award or pay guide for your job.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. To find your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates or allowances.

faqs.q: Does the salary calculator include super and tax?
faqs.a: Yes, the calculator estimates superannuation at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Tax is estimated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the full tax-free threshold, plus the Medicare levy of 2%. However, it does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. The result is an estimate only.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Use a Salary Calculator Australia to Compare Hourly and Annual Pay

Whether you’re negotiating a job offer, checking your current rate, or planning your budget, a **salary calculator Australia** is a handy tool. It lets you quickly convert an hourly rate into annual, fortnightly and weekly figures, and see how tax and super affect your take-home pay. This article explains the simple maths behind the calculator, explains the difference between the National Minimum Wage versus an award, and how to use the on-site timesheet on this site.

### The Simple Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The core calculation is straightforward: annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. Most full-time roles in Australia are based on 38 hours per week, as defined by the Fair Work Act. So if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, your annual gross is about $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44. Your weekly pay would be $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72, and fortnightly pay is double that: $2,009.44.

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances or salary sacrifice. If your hours vary, you may need to use an average. The calculator on this site uses this method and lets you enter your own base hourly rate.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor for all employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, many workers are covered by an award – a document that sets minimum pay rates and conditions for a specific industry or occupation. Award rates are often higher than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the Hospitality Industry General Award or the Clerks Private Sector Award have their own pay scales. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. Always check the correct award for your job before relying on the minimum wage.

When using a salary calculator Australia, you should enter your base hourly rate as stated in your award or contract. If you are a casual, the calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading on top of that base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading – let the calculator do the addition.

### Including Super and Tax

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual gross is $52,269, your employer would contribute an extra $6,272 in super (12% of $52,269). This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners, using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). The calculator estimates your tax and Medicare, but does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Using the Timesheet on This Site

The [timesheet](/) is the home page of this site. You type your base hourly rate into the field. If you are a casual employee, tick the checkbox that adds 25% casual loading. The calculator then shows:
- Annual gross pay (hourly × 38 × 52)
- Fortnightly pay (weekly × 2)
- Weekly pay
- Estimated tax and Medicare
- Estimated super (12% on top)

It also shows the National Minimum Wage for comparison. Remember, the calculator assumes a standard 38-hour week. If your hours are different, you can adjust the hours per week in the formula, but the on-site tool uses 38 hours as the default.

### A Note on Averages

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) figures. For May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week. That is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. These figures are useful for benchmarking but do not reflect what a particular job pays. For job-specific pay data, refer to the relevant award or the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [reference tables. See our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more details.

### Putting It All Together

A salary calculator Australia is a practical starting point. Use it to compare a job offer against the minimum wage, estimate your fortnightly budget, or see how much super you’ll accumulate. But always remember the disclaimer: the result is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay or tax. For precise figures, consult your employer, your award, or a qualified accountant. The Fair Work Commission sets the minimum wage, the ATO sets tax rates, and the ATO also handles super caps. This site provides the tools, but you should always verify with official sources.

Now head to the [timesheet](/) and try it yourself. Enter your hourly rate, tick casual loading if applicable, and see your annual, fortnightly and weekly pay with tax and super.
